For shared_buffers: on a dedicated DB server with ≥1GB RAM, start around 25% of system memory; rarely benefit from >40% and use smaller percentages on systems with <1GB. Increasing shared_buffers often implies increasing max_wal_size [1].

For effective_cache_size: it is only a planner-time estimate of the disk cache available to a single query (considers shared_buffers plus the OS cache and concurrent-query sharing); higher values favor index scans, lower values favor sequential scans. It does not allocate or reserve memory [2].
